text:
nora: running into a subtle issue in py-sdk 0.7.3 async: when server responds with a non-JSON error body the SDK tries to json.loads and we end up with a JSONDecodeError that gets wrapped into RedwoodAPIError but without HTTP status or the raw response attached. callers can't distinguish validation vs auth errors.

ishaan: can you paste the tiny repro and the raised exception text? async or sync?

nora: async. minimal repro:
```py
async with RedwoodClient(api_key=...) as client:
    await client.accounts.create({'company': 'X'})  # upstream returns 422 text/plain 'missing email'
```
exception shown in logs: `RedwoodAPIError: failed to parse error payload` and `hasattr(e, 'http_status')` is False. headers: `content-type: text/plain; charset=utf-8`, body: `missing email`

bree: that matches something I saw last month. sync path preserves error.raw_bytes + http_status, but async wrapper was re-raising a fresh RedwoodAPIError without copying attrs.

omar: quick proposal: in async response handler read raw_bytes = await resp.read() and populate a single instance of RedwoodAPIError with these attrs before trying to parse: `err.http_status = resp.status`, `err.raw_bytes = raw_bytes`, `err.raw_body = decoded_text_or_None`, `err.parsed_json = parsed or None`. If parsing fails, chain the JSONDecodeError as the __cause__ but still raise err with metadata. Keep public attr names stable: `http_status`, `raw_body`, `raw_bytes`, `parsed_json`.

ishaan: typing note: update .pyi to include those optionals: `http_status: Optional[int]`, `raw_body: Optional[str]`, `raw_bytes: Optional[bytes]`, `parsed_json: Optional[dict]`. Also add a small helper method `RedwoodAPIError.json()` that returns `parsed_json` or raises `MessageParseError('no json in body')`.

bree: also add a `body` property for compatibility that returns `raw_body` but emits DeprecationWarning. Some customers still access `.body` in their error handling.

omar: and protect __str__: if raw_body is > 2048 bytes, truncate and append `... (truncated)` to avoid logging huge binary pages. tests should assert this truncation behavior.

ci-bot: CI: feature/async-error-plumbing branch  tests failing (mypy: RedwoodAPIError missing attributes) <https://ci.internal/py-sdk/3456|details>

ishaan: tests to add: unit faked aiohttp response with `content-type: text/plain` ensuring `e.http_status == 422` and `e.raw_body == 'missing email'`; unit that simulates gzipped or binary body and asserts `raw_bytes` preserved and `raw_body` is None if decoding fails; mypy stub test to assert attributes exist. Also add integration test that triggers HTML error page via staging proxy.

bree: small implementation detail: decode with resp.get_encoding() or default to 'utf-8' with errors='replace', but still keep raw_bytes for exactness. public raw_body should always be str or None.

nora: perfect. is this a patch release?

omar: yes small bugfix -> target 0.7.4 patch. include changelog entry and update exceptions docs with pattern:
```py
try:\n    await client.accounts.create(...)
except RedwoodAPIError as e:\n    # robust handling\n    status = e.http_status\n    raw = e.raw_body\n    parsed = e.parsed_json\n    # prefer parsed_json when present, fall back to raw_body for legacy responses
```

ishaan: one more: ensure the JSON parsing is only attempted when content-type contains 'json' OR body startswith `{`/`[` to avoid false positives with proxied HTML pages that may include JSON-looking fragments.

bree: agree. and keep the original parse exception as cause so Sentry shows why parse failed.

ci-bot: CI: branch updated, lint OK, running tests + mypy. <https://ci.internal/py-sdk/3456|details>

nora: thanks all — i'll open the PR with tests + .pyi change and ping reviewers @ishaan @bree. leaving a curl to reproduce locally: `curl -i -X POST https://staging.api.redwood.com/v1/accounts -d '{"company":"X"}' -H "Content-Type: application/json"` returns `HTTP/1.1 422` with `text/plain` body on our staging proxy.

ishaan: :thumbsup:
